app.title: CADET-Equations: Model Equation Generator
app.summary: The person builds a column process model by picking options in a sidebar: column geometry and spatial resolution, dispersion, whether there are particles and of what kind, binding and reaction models, the parameter notation and the unit system. They can also load an earlier configuration file or a simulator model file to fill in the options. As options change, the main pane rewrites the full set of governing equations with boundary conditions and references, and shows which simulators support the model. Toggles add the model assumptions, a table of symbols with their units and descriptions. The person then downloads the equations as LaTeX or PDF, a simulator script template, or the configuration as JSON.

task.text: Build up a mathematical process model from modular choices and get back its governing equations, assumptions and symbol table, ready to put in a paper or a simulation.

data.text: A model configuration made of discrete modelling choices, which the app turns into a typeset document of equations, assumptions, a symbol table and references.
data.item: one model configuration (geometry, resolution, particle types, binding and reaction models) and the equation set generated from it

stage.text: formulating a process model before simulating it, and writing its equations up for a paper

mechanism.text: Dropdowns, toggles and number inputs in the sidebar set the model state. Each change re-renders the main pane as a typeset equation document with solver-support badges, plus an optional assumptions list and symbol table. The same content is collected as it renders, so it can be exported as LaTeX, PDF, a script template or a configuration file.

field.text: mechanistic modelling of packed-bed chromatography in chemical engineering

workflow.name: compose a model from modular options and generate its equations

steps.here: Optionally upload a saved JSON configuration or a simulator HDF5 model file. For an HDF5 file the person picks which unit to read, and its settings fill the session.

steps.step: choose the model's components from fixed options
steps.here: Sidebar dropdowns set column geometry and resolution, dispersion, particles or a size distribution, binding model and kinetics, and bulk and particle reactions. Developer mode opens a crystallization model family and per-component or per-particle-type settings.
Pick the CADET or legacy parameter notation and a unit system. Both change how every symbol is written.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The main pane assembles the governing PDEs, boundary conditions, binding and reaction terms and citations for the chosen configuration, and badges show whether each simulator supports it, supports it approximately or not at all.
Toggles show the model assumptions grouped by section and a symbol table with description, dependence, unit and an SI conversion factor.
Download model.tex, compile and download a PDF, download a simulator Python template, or generate and download the configuration as JSON to load again later.

distinctive: The output is typeset equations, not numbers: every option adds, drops or rewrites terms in the PDE system and its boundary conditions.
Solver-availability badges tell the person whether the configured model can actually be simulated in each simulator.
Assumptions and citations are generated along with the equations, so the write-up states what the model assumes and where each part comes from.
Configurations go both ways: they load from a simulator's own model file, and export as JSON or a runnable script template.
